why_three_counts: deny_rows_tested counts rows with a test and no residual gap. A row with a verified probe and a named gap is counted separately rather than folded into either side: folded up it overstates coverage, folded down it is indistinguishable from a row nobody has tested. The base-table deny row is the case that forced the distinction -- tests/e2_egress_d2d.py proves the column and row boundary AND proves its own grant probe moves, and still cannot observe consumer identity on this tier.
what_this_is: The matrix written down precisely enough to be disagreed with. PLAN_ONLY_NOT_APPLIED and PROVISIONAL are separate caveats: the first is a tier limit that a paid account removes, the second is a missing governance input that it does not.
what_this_is_not: Not a deployed control. 7 of 14 deny rows have no test at all, and they are the separation-of-duty rows -- untestable in a prototype where one operator wears every hat. This sentence previously counted 9 rows as untested, which was wrong once a deny row acquired a verified probe AND a named residual gap: that row has a test, and saying otherwise understated the one piece of internal-channel evidence E1 actually produced. The ARB package must distinguish three states, not two -- measured and clean, measured with a named gap, and a sentence nobody has tested.
